slot.brief: Given mass of a known nonelectrolyte dissolved in a solvent mass and Kf, compute the freezing point of the solution.

stem: A solution is prepared by dissolving $9.2$ g of glycerol (molar mass $92\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$) in $100$ g of water. Find its freezing point if $K_f=1.86\ ^\circ\text{C kg mol}^{-1}$ and pure water freezes at $0\ ^\circ\text{C}$.

verdicts.working: Moles of glycerol = 9.2/92 = 0.1 mol; molality = 0.1/0.1 = 1 mol kg⁻¹. Thus ΔTf = Kf m = 1.86 °C, so the solution freezes at −1.86 °C.

working:
$n=\dfrac{9.2}{92}=0.10$ mol; solvent mass $=0.100$ kg
$m=\dfrac{0.10}{0.100}=1.0$ mol kg$^{-1}$
$\Delta T_f=K_fm=1.86\ ^\circ\text{C}$
$T_f=0-1.86=-1.86\ ^\circ\text{C}$

Independent check: Moles of glycerol = 9.2/92 = 0.1 mol; molality = 0.1/0.1 = 1 mol kg⁻¹. Thus ΔTf = Kf m = 1.86 °C, so the solution freezes at −1.86 °C.
solution:
Moles of glycerol $=\frac{9.2}{92}=0.10$ mol; molality $=\frac{0.10}{0.100}=1.0\ \text{mol kg}^{-1}$.
$$\Delta T_f=K_fm=1.86\times1.0=1.86^\circ\text{C}$$
Hence, $T_f=0-1.86=-1.86^\circ\text{C}$.
